chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If obscenity had a form/resemblance, its resemblance would be evil.'

key_terms.الْفُحْشُ: Obscenity, immodesty, or foulness in speech and conduct
key_terms.مِثَالًا: A form, shape, or visual resemblance

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about the visual nature of obscenity?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s metaphor that obscenity (fuhsh) is so inherently repulsive that if it possessed a physical form, it would manifest as the epitome of ugliness. This emphasizes the aesthetic and spiritual dissonance of immodesty in speech and conduct, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings on refining character (akhlaq).
